title: 227 tests passed and the bot finished the level, but my UE 5.9 jam game ignored most real mouse clicks
author: VictorBuildsApps
selftext:
BREAK THE HOST is my entry for the Epic AI MegaJam: a short top-down action game in Unreal Engine 5.9, C++ with GAS. You get a sword, a dodge and a gauntlet that throws enemy soldiers into their own ranks. AI coding agents wrote the code and drove the editor. I directed, played the builds and decided what shipped.

On the last day I played a release candidate, and my note was "problems attacking and fighting, it was just not working". All 227 automated tests had passed, and nine of ten full bot runs had finished the route (the tenth stalled in the boss fight, a separate issue). None of them could catch it, because the bot and the tests call the attack in code. A player's click goes through the game window first.

The cause: the cursor stays visible in play because the crosshair aims with it. With a visible cursor, Unreal's viewport releases mouse capture on every button release. Under the default Game Only input mode, the next press is spent taking capture back and never reaches Enhanced Input. So after the first click, almost every sword and gauntlet press was eaten, unless it was a fast double click.

The fix is one input mode for every way back into play (Begin, resume from pause, checkpoint restart, closing the shrine menu): Game Only with SetConsumeCaptureMouseDown(false). A test now fails if any other Game Only input mode shows up in the game code.

The agents also needed a check that goes through the window like a player does. It starts at the title, presses Begin, posts real Windows mouse-down and mouse-up messages to the game window, and counts the swing and gauntlet sounds in the game's audio log. The broken build swung on 1 of 6 clicks and threw on 0 of 2. The fixed build got 6 of 6 and 2 of 2, then 6 of 6 and 1 of 1 after a pause, then fought for 40 seconds with every swing and throw coming from a click. Now they run it after any input or screen change. The clip is a later bot run on the released build's content.

If your agents run playtest bots, do the bots send input through the window, or call the game's functions directly?

comments.author: biggdogg420
comments.body: I’d add one case where the window loses focus mid-level and the player returns before pressing attack. The first click after the window is active again is a different path from Begin or Resume, and your sound counter could tell you immediately if capture ate that click too.

replies.author: VictorBuildsApps
replies.body: Good call, that path isn't covered. The check only clicks after Begin and after pause/resume. Focus loss and return was on the list of rechecks after the fix and never made it into the script. The fix sets the capture mode that also passes on the click that takes capture, so it should get through, but nothing has tested it yet.
